chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Cure your sick with charity, and ward off calamity with supplication, and bring down provision with charity, for indeed it loosens the jaws of seven hundred devils, and nothing is heavier upon the devil than charity upon the believer, and it falls in the hand of the Lord (Exalted) before it falls in the hand of the servant.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of charity and supplication in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links charity (sadaqah) directly to divine protection and sustenance, noting its unique status as being in God's hand even before reaching the recipient's. The narration highlights the metaphysical weight of sadaqah against devils, reinforcing the Shia scholarly view that charitable acts serve as both spiritual purification and a tangible shield against calamity (balā').
